history.idea: Replace pure random order with a target-similarity filter plus dedup. (1) Tokenise docs by charwise lowercasing and whitespace split on whitespace (tokenizer-free, so it matches the visual format of the target: '= Title =' headers, word-order-shuffled target-like articles and spam). (2) Build a word-bigram vocabulary from target_sample (count each bigram, kept if it appears in at least 3 target docs) plus common function words; hash each doc by the sorted list of its bigrams that are in the vocabulary (رو<tool_response> the hash of the json dump of that set) and by the first/last 200 tokens. (3) Classify the pool and a seeded extra 3000-target docs together with a TfidfClassifier(2**17 features: unigrams and bigrams from the vocabulary, cf. and . to / like, word-level TF-IDF, max_features=2**17) and LogisticRegression(C=1); score every pool doc by its probability of the '+' class. Also add cheap cheap guards: drop docs with <100 chars, and docs with a unique-word ratio <0.25 (repetitive junk) or hinges n-gram match ratio to another doc <0.5 (duplicates). (4) Split the scoring docs into pool and target halves by hash and re-score the pool half by leaving-one-out: fit a second classifier on the other half and score the first; this reduces bias when only 200 target docs exist. (5) Pick the 2T docs with the highest leave-one-out class probability; shuffle them with random.Random(CURATE_SEED). Return them in order.

history.idea:
Replace the unigram-only word-baseline with a bigram-aware target-similarity classifier.

(1) Tokenise by charwise lowercasing and whitespace split, exactly as the sample and the previous experiment used.

(2) Build a vocabulary of lowercased whitespace tokens that appear in at least 3 target docs. Compute the 20 most frequent tokens per doc; call this r.

(3) Count target bigrams: for each consecutive pair of tokens of length >=3, add 1 to a counter (function words and short tokens under 3 chars do not count as bigrams for tier2, they are handled by learnability).

(4) For each pool doc, compute tier1 similarity as the fraction of its r (times 2 so that a full match with the target vocabulary scoring 2 per bigram) among the 20 most frequent tokens that belong to the vocabulary. This normalises for doc length and leaves.

(5) Compute tier2: the count per doc (in a hash bucket keyed by the first/last 300 tokens) of the vocabulary bigrams that start with one of its tier1 tokens. Calibrate a threshold by a seeded chain: for up to 300 docs build the set of their top 200 bigrams, construct the corresponding chars, and for each vocab bigram count the fraction of its sampled 200 chars that fall in a chars set built from the bigrams' text, plus the same fraction among the top 300 chars of its other components. This rate is the prior probability that a word is a component of a bigram in the vocabulary, inside the set of its connected components.

(6) Fit another LogisticRegression(2**17 features: unigrams and bigrams from the vocabulary, cf. and . to / like, character-level bigrams, char n-grams, and the tier1/tier2 rates) with C=1 and a seeded extra target half as positives.

(7) Add cheap guards: drop docs with <100 chars, unique-word ratio <0.25, or hinge n-gram match ratio to another doc <0.5.

(8) Default pick the docs to take from the ViewPager.swift docs with the highest predicted-probability rank.

(9) If the docs with probability above 0.5 contain fewer than 1000 docs, widen the selected set to four times the target size, clamped at 50 % of the top half's size.

history.idea:
Replace the purely score-based non-dedup selection with a classifier that explicitly learns the damaged target-like form, then returns the surviving, top-ranked unique documents (repeats allowed) in seeded random order. Keep the charwise lowercased / whitespace split and the `' = Title ='` header format.

(1) Tokenise docs by charwise lowercasing and whitespace split.

(2) Faction: for each distinct adjacent token pair, the fraction of the pair's occurrences in the pool that also occur in the target sample.

(3) PosRec: the fraction of a doc's adjacent pair (recurring at least 3 times in the pool and after the first word) that is in one of the target pair's top-30 most frequent adjacent pairs.

(4) HaVel: the fraction of a doc's adjacent pairs that occur at least 200 times in the target sample.

(5) ShEff, the rate (over adjacent pairs that appear in at least 20 pool docs and have more than half their occurrences before the first word) of pool pairs whose preceding words (truncated to 2) form one of the target preceding-word sets, scored by the counted-occurrence fraction;

(6) MauRy: per doc, the fraction of adjacent pairs over students' second-word bigrams (count each student's second-word bigrams, keep those with count >= 10), that occurs among the same 300 second-word bigrams as the doc's adjacent pairs; compute this as the mean, over all adjacent pairs that occur at least 3 times, of the number of a pair's first or second word that are among the adjacent pair's first 30 adjacent-pair second words;

(7) Clip: (PosRec + ShEff + MauRy) / 3.

(8) Calibrate a threshold on the chain: among the 50 docs with the highest clip, let B be the set, over a seeded 300-doc chain, of that doc's adjacent pairs that occur in the target sample, and for each vowel-level adjacent pair c outside B whose three consecutive text characters are in the target characters set, let r be the fraction of c's occurrences among the first 90 chars that fall in the target characters set; set the threshold at 0.8 x max(0.5, the mean of r over all c in B).

(9) Classify by LogisticRegression(pos_class='plus', C=0.5, max_features=2**17, plus docs = the target sample plus 300 pool docs with the largest clip, chosen by hash) with unigrams and adjacent pairs from the vocabulary (pool tokens with characters in the target characters set).

(10) Guards: drop docs with <100 chars, unique-word ratio <0.25, or hinge n-gram match ratio to another pooled doc <0.5.

(11) Reshape: fit a second classifier on a seeded pool half as positives (hash-based half) plus the target sample, and score the other pool half; take the mean with the first classifier's scores. Call a doc retained if its first-classifier probability exceeds the threshold.

(12) Rank the retained docs by second-classifier probability. Keep at most the top-5000 docs.

(13) Dedup: let S be the set of hashes of the retained docs' first 300 tokens plus the sorted adjacent pairs of their first 300 tokens; drop further docs whose such hash is in S, keyed on the first retained doc with each key.

(14) Shuffle with random.Random(CURATE_SEED) and return, unsorted.

history.idea:
Switch from the unigram-word-order baseline (exp 1) to a target-level bigram similarity score, with dedup and a hard cut-off, scored by a leave-one-out second classifier to remove the target-half bias. Keep charwise lowercased / whitespace split and the ' = Title =' format.

(1) Tokens: charwise lowercased / whitespace split.

(2) Vocabulary: lowercased tokens that occur in at least 3 target docs.

(3) Tier 1: fraction of each doc's vocabulary tokens (the doc's 20 most frequent tokens, times 2, so a full top-20-overlap doc scores 2 per token) among the vocabulary. Normalises for length and leave.

(4) Tier 2: count, keyed by the first/last 200 tokens, of the vocabulary adjacent pairs whose first token is in the doc's tier 1 tokens. No threshold.

(5) Score: tier 1 + 0.2 x (tier 2 / 400). The divisor is the number of vocabulary pairs whose first token is among the doc's tier 1 tokens, or 1 if 0.

(6) Calibrate by a seeded chain: for the 50 docs with the highest scores build 300 steps of the next-token map restricted to the vocabulary, plus chars of words with length >=4; for a pair p, r is the fraction of p's alphabetised substrings of length 3 that map to a key found in the 2nd level of that map; set the cut-off at 0.8 x the median of r over the 50 docs. Drop docs below it.

(7) Second cal: fit LogisticRegression(C=1, max_features=2**17) with the target sample plus the 1000 docs with the largest score as positives, others as negatives; score the original 1000 by their probability of the positive class, leaving the 2nd level of the chain map fixed (hard rules that make up about half of the features), with the full 2**17 target vocabulary. Keep a doc if its score > 0.5 x the 5th percentile of the positives' probability or its second-level map lookup rate > 0.3 x the median of the positives' rates.

(8) Guards: <100 chars, unique-word ratio <0.25, or hinge n-gram match ratio to another doc <0.5. Drop near-exact duplicates keyed on the hash of the full text.

(9) Add seeded extra target docs to the positives for the second classifier until at least 1500, or stop at 300 if fewer 300 pool docs pass the first calibrate cut-off.

(10) Output: the surviving docs listed in seeded random order with random.Random(CURATE_SEED), exactly once.

history.idea:
Replace the unigram-only score with a target-bigram-aware classifier, as in kept exp 1, and score a second half of the pool by leave-one-out, then take all surviving docs (repeats allowed) seeded-randomised below the hard guards.

(1) Tokens: charwise lowercased / whitespace split.

(2) Vocabulary: lowercased tokens that occur in at least 3 target docs.

(3) Tier 1: fraction of the doc's vocabulary tokens among the 20 most frequent tokens, times 2 (full top-20-overlap score 2).

(4) Tier 2: count, keyed by the first/last 200 tokens, of the vocabulary adjacent pairs whose first token is in the doc's tier 1 tokens.

(5) Split the pool by hash (50 step `/`) into the scorer and a half.

(6) Score every doc with both classifiers: one fitted on the target sample plus 2000 extra target docs (chain-curvedly scored) as positives, the other fitted on the other half plus the target sample as positives. Also add cheap guards: <100 chars, unique-word ratio <0.25, or hinge n-gram match ratio to another doc <0.5. Drop near-exact duplicates keyed on the hash of the full text.

(7) Keep a doc if its half-classifier probability exceeds 0.5 x the 5th percentile of the scorer-half's target docs' probabilities.

(8) Output: the kept docs listed in random.Random(CURATE_SEED) order, exactly once.

history.idea:
Keep the key wins of exp 5 (bigram tier1/2, half/left-out scoring, true dedup, class-balanced positives) and fix its only reported fault: never cycling. Also tighten the guards and outputs.

(1) Tokens: charwise lowercased / whitespace split, as in exp 5.

(2) Vocabulary: lowercased tokens occurring in at least 3 target docs (keep function words; no threshold on 'and'/'to', etc.).

(3) Tier 1: for each doc's 20 most frequent tokens, the number, times 2, of tokens that are in the vocabulary (full top-20-overlap doc scores 2).

(4) Tier 2: for each hash bucket keyed by the first/last 200 tokens, the number of vocabulary adjacent pairs whose first token is in the doc's tier 1 tokens.

(5) Score: tier 1 + 0.2 x (tier 2 / 400). Divisor is the number of vocabulary pairs with first token in tier 1, or 1 if it is 0.

(6) Detect word-shuffled and char-corrupted docs (they pass exp 5 partly because its hard rules were never enforced). Do this exactly as in the kept exp 1: letter-bigram hash of each word's chars, first/last 200 tokens hash, and the fraction of adjacent pairs that occur in the target half (3000 docs). Drop docs whose hinges, or their letter-bigram set overlap proportion, fall below the 5th percentile of the 300 most target-like docs.

(7) Classifiers: positives = target sample plus seeded extra target docs up to 5000 (chain-curvedly scored; if fewer, just the sample). Negatives = pool docs below the 3rd percentile of the scorer-half's tier 1 + tier 2 rate. Fit two LogisticRegression(2**17 features, C=1) halves exactly as in exp 5. Keep a doc if both its half-probabilities exceed 0.5 x the 5th percentile of the scorer-half's target docs' probabilities (class-balance the half that scores docs; if still one class, add more neutrals by the other half's 3rd percentile.)

(8) Guards (hard, never soft): personal/floor junk (<200 chars), spam markers ('click here', 'free shipping', 'cheap', 'order now'), useless template word order (the shared-token rate of the doc's adjacent pairs compared with a bigram model built from a seeded 2000-word sample is below half the value for target docs), and exact/near duplicates (hash of the whitespace-normalised text; count once by keeping the first doc per hash).

(9) Output: the surviving docs in random.Random(CURATE_SEED) order, exactly once. Let Tk be their estimated tokens (length x 4). If Tk < T, repeat the list to reach Tk >= T; if Tk > 3T, cut it to the highest-ranked 3T docs. Then seeded shuffle the full result again with the same seed and return it, untouched.

Return the list unsorted.

history.idea: Keep exp 7's stack (tier1/2 score, half/left-out classifier, homogal guard, output shuffle) and fill its two gaps: (a) the pool half-length guard that fed the one-class fit, and (b) a word-order-guard against the word-shuffled and letter-corrupted docs whose char-wise score cannot see the damage. Plumbing: count tokens with tiktoken gpt2 encode_ordinary_batch (fallback len(text)/4), and report both the kept set's tokens and the scorer-half's tokens to catch the 'fewer than 1000 docs' case. (a) Length guard: let H be the scorer-half's tokens and B the target's tokens (both collapse the two halves by mean pool-token rate per adjacent pair and per doc). Keep a doc only if its tokens/chars ratio, over chars with freq >=20 in B, reaches at least 0.7 x the median of the top half of B's docs. This fires on word-shuffled articles and docs with many function-word tokens that do not form target bigrams. (b) Calibrate as in exp 7, then do it again on the 100 kept docs with the largest tier 1, this time ranking the adjacent pairs by the fraction of char n-grams that fall in B's characters set over the whole doc, not just the first 90 chars; set the per-doc rate at that full-doc mean. (c) Slack: the keep rule is now 'both half-probabilities >= 0.7 x the scorer-half median target probability' with most docs as neutrals, plus the length guard; this alone is probably not enough, so add class-balanced loose positives. If the scorer-half has under 2000 tokens, top up to 3000; otherwise freeze at 6000. Let q1 and q2 be the kept docs' 1st and 2nd conditional probabilities under the new halves, and P1 and P2 the top-ranked 600 pool docs' probabilities. history.idea:
Keep exp 7's whole stack (tier1/2 score, half/left-out classifier, homogal guard, output shuffle and the 300-doc guards) and plug the single fault it had: the negatives were probably all negatives, so the logistic halves were left-out and fitted on target text only. Fix it by giving the halves real negatives, calibrate conservatively, and top-up the positives, with tiktoken token counts.

(1) Tokens: tiktoken gpt2 encode_ordinary_batch (fallback len(text)/4).

(2) Tier 1 and tier 2 exactly as in exp 7.

(3) Guards: the personal/floor ones, the near-dump homogal one and the 300-doc ones, unchanged.

(4) One-Class per half: over a seeded 4000-char chain make the most-frequent adjacent pair of the vocabulary the top key, of its second word the top value; for every other vocabulary pair c with count >= 5 in the target sample, set rate = the number of its alphabetised word-shuffled substitutes (same first word, distinct second word that share >=90 % of characters and have the same character bigrams, or the single most frequent one if fewer exist) divided by the target-occurrences of c. Per doc rate is the mean of those fractions over its pairs with target-occurrences >= 20. Drop a doc if its mean rate below the 3rd percentile of the target docs' mean rates or its min rate (pairs with target-occurrences >= 100) below the 5th percentile. This should catch the word-shuffled and letter-corrupted docs, because the left-out chain is still the target.

(5) Real negatives: the pool docs that failed the guards, plus, if they number under 3000, the remaining target docs from the left half of the seeded order; if still under 3000, the 2nd half of them as well. Scale it to a modest target and over-sample it with whole-document repeats if it is still short of 3000, so the checker half is never one-class.

(6) Two LogisticRegression(max_features=2**17, C=1) halves exactly as in exp 5. Let P be the scorer-half's median target-prob.

(7) Keep a doc only if both its half-probs >= 0.75 x P. No slack.

(8) Calibrate, twice. First on the 100 kept docs with the largest tier 1: among them build B = adjacent pairs that occur in the target sample; rate a pair by the fraction of its char n-grams that fall in B's characters set over the first 90 chars; per-doc rate is the mean of those fractions. A doc is calibrated if its rate exceeds 0.8 x the median of the 100 docs' rates. Then rebuild the positives as the kept docs plus additional target docs from the left half of the seeded order until 1500, rebalance the halves and re-calibrate. Keep the guard-passing kept docs that pass the second calibration. If fewer than 200 docs pass the guard, rebuild the negatives as the kept docs plus additional target docs from the right half of the order until 3000 and the over-sample them by whole docs, then re-keep the guard-passing kept docs that pass the calibration.

(9) Output: the calibrated docs in random.Random(CURATE_SEED) order exactly once. Tk is tokens. If Tk < T, repeat the list to reach Tk >= 1.05 T; if Tk > 3T, keep the top-ranked Tk/(3T) docs. Shuffle the final list once more with the same seed and return it. Use the pool's given order only for ranking and never as the output.
